slicer_intro: Kobralink exposes every printer as a Moonraker server. OrcaSlicer connects to it like a Klipper machine: direct print upload, live monitoring, ACE filament sync.
slicer_addresses_hint: Each printer has its own port. Replace “machine-ip” with the IP address of the machine running Kobralink (or localhost if OrcaSlicer runs on the same machine), then paste it into OrcaSlicer's “Host” field.
slicer_addresses_empty: No printer configured yet. Add one from the home page to get its address.
slicer_step_1: In the Prepare tab, click the connection (plug) icon next to the printer preset, or open Printer settings → General → Physical printer.
slicer_step_3: Hostname / IP / URL: paste the address above, replacing “machine-ip” with the IP address of the machine running Kobralink (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:7125), or with localhost if OrcaSlicer runs on the same machine (http://localhost:7125). Keep the protocol (http://, or https:// if a TLS reverse proxy sits in front of Kobralink) and the port. API key: leave empty by default; if you enabled "Require an API key" below, paste a key generated here.
slicer_step_4: Click Test: OrcaSlicer should report “Connection succeeded”. Save; the Device tab now shows your Kobra and the Print button sends the G-code to Kobralink.
slicer_note_scope: The OrcaSlicer Device tab only targets the printer: start a print, follow progress, pause or cancel, sync the ACE filaments. Everything else (queue, files, macros, per-slot profiles, camera, failure detection, statistics, notifications, API keys) is managed here, in Kobralink.
slicer_note_running: Kobralink must be running for OrcaSlicer to connect: with the desktop app, keep the window open (or minimised) while sending.
slicer_note_firewall: If OrcaSlicer runs on another machine, the firewall must allow the printer's port. On the same machine, http://localhost:{port} works too.
slicer_note_ams: The filament sync button in the Device tab fetches the ACE slots. The profile sent per slot is set in the printer settings (OrcaSlicer profile).
slicer_keys_hint: By default the Moonraker ports are open to the whole LAN, like Moonraker itself. Enable the option to require a key (X-Api-Key header) on every request: OrcaSlicer, Fluidd, Obico and Home Assistant support it. Keys are managed in Settings → API keys, with the Moonraker use.
slicer_keys_require: Require an API key on Moonraker ports
slicer_keys_require_hint: Applies to every printer, camera included (/api/camera/*). Mainsail cannot enter an API key.
api_keys_delete_hint: Software using it will no longer be able to connect.

api_keys_use_mcp_hint: An MCP key always covers every printer.
api_key_bad_scope: Invalid key uses: tick at least one use, a single MCP access, and an MCP key must cover every printer.

slicer_keys_camera_hint: For a camera stream without headers (img tag), append ?api_key=<key> to the URL.
